answer: I would tie each agent to one registered ship. First, the agent pins its public key to a vessel's IMO number in the global registry. Second, the network checks the registry and bars a second agent on the same hull. Third, a yearly AIS ping proves the ship still sails, or the seat goes dark. Fielding 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 ships at $200,000 each for the smallest coastal trader, $200 million before one fake earns a cent. A lantern on a real ship is easy to check from shore. An ocean of fake names has no hull behind it, and a fake fleet never reaches the horizon.
